name: Ethics, Rules of Conduct and professionalism
description: Professional conduct as a regulated member: RICS Rules of Conduct, conflicts of interest, client money, professional indemnity and the general principles of law in your jurisdiction (Canadian provinces, US states).
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of RICS Rules of Conduct, ethical principles, professional standards, and the importance of ethical behavior in surveying practice.
l2: Demonstrate application of ethical principles and RICS Rules of Conduct through specific examples, including identification of ethical issues and appropriate action taken.
l3: Demonstrate ability to provide reasoned advice on complex ethical matters, exercise professional judgment in ethical dilemmas, navigate conflicts of interest, and uphold the highest standards of professional conduct.
l4: Sits on a disciplinary or standards body (RICS Regulatory Tribunal, an AIC or state appraisal board panel) or writes conduct guidance that other professionals are held to.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph

name: Client care
description: Meeting a client's brief and managing the relationship: terms of engagement, understanding needs, service standards, complaints handling, and treating every stakeholder in an appointment as a client.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of client care principles, service standards, professional obligations to clients, and the importance of meeting client needs
l2: Demonstrate application of client care principles through specific examples of managing client relationships, delivering professional service, handling client concerns, and ensuring client satisfaction
l3: Provide reasoned advice to clients and stakeholders on service standards, engagement terms, complaint handling and relationship management, and evaluate client feedback to improve how service is delivered.
l4: Writes the client-care or complaints-handling standard other firms adopt (terms of engagement, complaints procedure, redress), or is engaged by other firms to review escalated complaints.
source: L1-L2: RICS-APC-prep; L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Communication and negotiation
description: Communicating in writing, graphically and orally, and planning and conducting negotiations: preparation, strategy, tactics and closing.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of effective communication techniques, negotiation principles, and stakeholder management
l2: Demonstrate application of communication and negotiation skills through specific examples including presentations, negotiations, written communications, and stakeholder engagement
l3: Evaluate your own written, graphic and oral communication and negotiation across varied settings, such as fee agreements, complex negotiations, stakeholder presentations and public speaking, and adapt your approach from what you learn.
l4: Brought in by other firms or clients to lead their hardest negotiations (portfolio deals, expropriation or lease settlements), or teaches negotiation on accredited courses.
source: L1-L2: RICS-APC-prep; L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Health and safety
description: The legal, practical and regulatory side of health and safety in a surveyor's work: occupational health and safety law (Ontario's OHSA, US OSHA rules), risk assessment, site safety and duties to others.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of health and safety legislation, risk assessment principles, and safety responsibilities
l2: Demonstrate application of health and safety principles through specific examples of conducting risk assessments, implementing control measures, and ensuring site safety compliance
l3: Give reasoned advice to clients and others on health and safety across your work, from occupational health and safety legislation and site hazards to safe systems of work and incident response.
l4: Writes the safety programme or guidance others work under (an industry association, a CSA or ANSI committee), or investigates and gives expert evidence on site incidents.
source: L1-L2: RICS-APC-prep; L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025), typo corrected; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Accounting principles and procedures
description: Basic accounting and reading company accounts (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow) under IFRS, ASPE or US GAAP, so that advice on a party's financial standing is sound.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of basic accounting principles, financial statements (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow), budgeting processes, and cost control
l2: Interpret financial statements, including balance sheets and income statements, for properties and companies in your field, and apply the accounting standards that govern them (IFRS, ASPE or US GAAP) and related reporting requirements.
l3: Give reasoned advice to clients on what income statements and balance sheets show about a party's financial strength, for example a tenant's covenant, a purchaser or a borrower, and on the preparation of property and entity accounts.
l4: Advises boards, audit committees or lenders outside their firm on property companies' accounts (IAS 40 investment property, IFRS 16 or ASC 842 leases), or teaches accounts analysis on professional programmes.
source: L1: RICS-APC-prep; L2-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Business planning
description: The principles and tools of business planning: objectives, market and competitor analysis, resource and financial planning, and measuring performance against the plan.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of business planning principles, strategic planning frameworks, business objectives, and resource management.
l2: Demonstrate practical application of business planning principles through setting objectives, preparing plans, analyzing performance, and using business planning tools in real work contexts.
l3: Demonstrate ability to provide professional advice to clients and senior stakeholders on business planning principles, evaluate business plan effectiveness, recommend strategic adjustments, and guide organizational decision-making.
l4: Prepares or challenges business plans for property or professional-services businesses other than their own (as adviser, director or investor), and others rely on the plan's market and financial assumptions.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph

name: Conflict avoidance, management and dispute resolution procedures
description: Recognising, avoiding, managing and resolving disputes, and the main procedures: negotiation, mediation, arbitration, expert determination and litigation.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of conflict avoidance strategies, dispute resolution methods (ADR, mediation, arbitration, litigation), and conflict management principles
l2: Apply conflict avoidance strategies in practice. Assist in dispute resolution processes. Identify appropriate dispute resolution methods for specific situations. Implement formal procedures for conflict management.
l3: Provide strategic advice on dispute avoidance and resolution. Act as mediator, adjudicator, arbitrator or expert determiner. Provide expert witness evidence. Advise on optimal dispute resolution strategy considering cost, time, risk and relationship factors.
l4: Sits on a dispute-resolution panel (ADR Institute of Canada, American Arbitration Association, RICS Dispute Resolution Service) and takes appointments from parties outside their firm, or writes dispute rules or guidance.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph

name: Data management
description: How project and practice data are collected, stored, secured and retrieved, and the privacy law that governs them (PIPEDA and provincial acts in Canada, state laws in the US).
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of privacy law (PIPEDA and provincial privacy acts in Canada; state laws such as the CCPA in the US), data security principles, information management systems, and data governance frameworks applicable to surveying practice.
l2: Apply data management knowledge in practical work situations, implement data protection measures, manage information systems, and handle data in compliance with regulations and professional standards.
l3: Provide strategic advice on data management, information governance, and data protection compliance. Lead organizational data protection initiatives, advise on complex data protection issues, and establish robust information management frameworks.
l4: Sets an organisation's records and privacy programme (retention schedules, access controls, breach response under PIPEDA or state law) and is consulted by peers outside it on data governance.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11)

name: Diversity, inclusion and teamworking
description: Working in and helping build diverse teams: inclusion, team roles and dynamics, human rights and employment-equity duties, and contributing to shared goals.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of diversity and inclusion principles, grounds protected under human rights law (for example the Ontario Human Rights Code and US Title VII), collaborative working, team roles and dynamics, and inclusive practices
l2: Work effectively as a member of a team in day-to-day practice, sharing information, supporting colleagues and applying inclusive behaviors in project work.
l3: Evaluate how well you work in and contribute to teams across different situations, including diverse and multidisciplinary teams, and act on what you learn to improve team performance.
l4: Designs inclusion practices (recruitment, mentoring, team norms) that other firms or an industry body adopt, with measured results, and advises on them beyond their organisation.
source: L1: RICS-APC-prep; L2-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Inclusive environments
description: Principles and processes that deliver accessible and inclusive environments, recognising the diversity of users and requirements such as AODA, the ADA and accessibility codes.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of accessibility requirements, inclusive design principles, equitable access, disability legislation, and community benefits
l2: Apply accessibility and inclusive-design principles and processes in your work, for example barrier-free design requirements under building codes and accessibility legislation such as the ADA or AODA.
l3: Give reasoned advice to clients and project teams on achieving accessible and inclusive environments, including compliance with accessibility legislation, barrier-free design standards and the needs of the people who will use the space.
l4: Audits other owners' buildings as a recognised accessibility assessor (such as Rick Hansen Foundation certification), or sits on a committee for standards such as CSA B651 or ICC A117.1.
source: L1: RICS-APC-prep; L2-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Sustainability
description: The surveyor's role in sustainability: climate change, energy, resource use, environmental impact and ESG, and how they affect property, land and construction.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of sustainability principles, environmental impact assessment, climate change context, renewable energy, and ESG factors
l2: Apply sustainability principles to projects, conduct environmental assessments, implement sustainable design/construction practices, and measure sustainability performance
l3: Provide strategic sustainability advice, develop organizational sustainability strategies, lead Net Zero initiatives, and advise on ESG integration
l4: Writes or reviews sustainability standards or guidance (CaGBC Zero Carbon Building, GRESB, RICS whole life carbon assessment) or leads net-zero programmes that others benchmark against.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph

name: Building control inspections
description: Inspecting building work at stages of construction for compliance with the building code (National Building Code of Canada, provincial codes, the International Building Code) and the orders and enforcement that follow non-compliance.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how construction is inspected at key stages of the work to confirm compliance with the building code, permits and related legislation, and of the scope and purpose of those inspections.
l2: Practical application of regulatory requirements through site inspections, assessment of construction work, identification of non-compliance, and appropriate enforcement action.
l3: Expert assessment of complex building projects, provision of detailed compliance advice with options appraisal, formal enforcement action including issuing orders (orders to comply, unsafe building orders), and professional judgment on unsafe buildings.
l4: Sits on a code development committee (Canadian Commission on Building and Fire Codes, ICC), issues code interpretations other officials rely on, or gives expert evidence in compliance disputes.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Fire safety
description: How fire behaves in buildings and how its effects are controlled: fire science, means of egress, compartmentation, fire safety engineering and strategy, and the codes that apply (National Fire Code of Canada, NFPA codes).
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of what fire does in a building, how the building's enclosure changes its behavior and how its effects are contained, and how fire safety principles reduce risk to life, property and the environment.
l2: Assess means of egress and fire safety management systems for specific buildings, drawing on how combustion works, the physics and chemistry of fire, and how fire affects people.
l3: Advise clients or other bodies on fire safety engineering needs and strategy, and act for clients before the authority having jurisdiction when a fire safety strategy is prepared, negotiated and defended.
l4: Sits on fire code or standards committees (NFPA, Canadian Commission on Building and Fire Codes), or gives expert evidence on fire strategies and fire losses in litigation.
source: L1, L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025), adapted for the graph; L2: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Inspection
description: Inspecting property for a purpose: what to record, the factors that shape an inspection, and turning findings into reports, schedules and advice.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of why and how properties are inspected, the information to gather beforehand, safety and access considerations, and how the property type and purpose shape the inspection approach.
l2: Carry out property inspections and use what you record to prepare reports, schedules or equipment inventories, presenting site, building and condition findings accurately.
l3: Give reasoned advice and recommendations based on your inspections, for example on condition, defects, marketability or value, and make clients aware of obligations the findings raise.
l4: Writes inspection standards or protocols others use (ASTM E2018 property condition assessments, a lender's inspection protocol), and trains and reviews other inspectors.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Legal/regulatory compliance
description: The laws and regulations that govern your area of practice (professional licensing, anti-money-laundering rules under FINTRAC or FinCEN, privacy, consumer protection) and how to comply with them in specific situations.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the statutes, regulations, codes and bylaws that govern your field, such as property law, zoning, building codes and occupational health and safety.
l2: Apply that knowledge to meet legal and regulatory requirements in specific assignments, drawing on current legislation, case law and regulatory guidance.
l3: Give reasoned written advice and present reports to clients on legal and regulatory compliance in your field, working with legal counsel where needed.
l4: Writes compliance policies or training that other firms follow (anti-money-laundering, licensing, privacy), or advises regulators and industry bodies on new rules for the profession.
source: L1: RICS-APC-prep; L2-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: BIM management
description: The technical, process and collaborative sides of building information modelling (BIM): ISO 19650, BIM execution plans, information requirements and common data environments.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of building information modeling: the technology, the processes and the collaboration it depends on, including data capture, classification systems and relevant standards.
l2: Set up and run the management processes that support BIM on projects, such as BIM execution plans, protocols, shared control and reporting procedures, and upkeep of the information model.
l3: Advise clients or senior management on BIM strategy at the corporate or project level, drawing on your experience to compare solutions and explain their contractual, commercial and technical implications.
l4: Writes BIM standards or templates adopted beyond their team (ISO 19650 guidance, the US National BIM Standard, buildingSMART Canada work), or sets an owner's BIM requirements for major programmes.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Building pathology
description: Building defects: how they arise, how to diagnose their causes, their consequences, and how to remedy them.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of building defects, their causes and effects, the types of surveys used to find them, and the testing methods available and their limits.
l2: Apply knowledge to identify causes and mechanics of building failures, explain relationships between observations and diagnosis, and gather information from multiple sources including specialist inspections.
l3: Providing expert diagnostic advice on complex or unusual building defects, explaining causes and consequences with comprehensive remedial recommendations, and preparing detailed schedules of works with cost-benefit analysis.
l4: Gives expert evidence on building defects in litigation or insurance claims, or publishes diagnostic guidance (building envelope, moisture, concrete deterioration) that other practitioners use.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Conservation and restoration
description: Conserving and restoring historic buildings and structures: conservation principles, investigation, suitable repair techniques and materials, and heritage protection (provincial heritage acts, the US National Register and state historic preservation review).
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of heritage conservation and restoration principles, techniques and materials, including heritage designation, identifying the age and style of structures, and the difference between conserving and restoring.
l2: Inspect and investigate a heritage building or structure to identify what affects its conservation or restoration, for example its materials, period of construction, condition and heritage approvals.
l3: Provide expert advice on conservation philosophy, appropriate interventions, and complex heritage conservation projects.
l4: Advises heritage authorities on designations and alterations, or writes guidance others follow under the Standards and Guidelines for the Conservation of Historic Places in Canada or the US Secretary of the Interior's Standards.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15); L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Construction technology and environmental services
description: Construction methods, building elements and environmental (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) services, through design and delivery, and the codes that govern them.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of construction methods, building elements, environmental services systems, design stages, and relevant legislation/regulations.
l2: Apply construction technology knowledge to real projects. Prepare technical details and specifications. Coordinate with MEP consultants. Assess buildability and alternative construction solutions. Ensure regulatory compliance.
l3: Provide strategic advice on construction methodology selection. Lead value engineering exercises. Advise on complex technical solutions with cost/programme/quality trade-offs. Resolve technical interface issues. Provide expert advice on building performance, sustainability strategies, and innovative construction approaches.
l4: Develops technical standards or master specifications others adopt (CSA, ASTM or ASHRAE committees), or is consulted by other firms on novel systems such as mass timber or deep envelope retrofits.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11)

name: Contaminated land
description: How land becomes contaminated, the liability and value effects, and how it is assessed and remediated: Phase I and II environmental site assessments (CSA Z768, ASTM E1527), records of site condition and remediation options.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how sites become contaminated, by human activity or natural causes, and what contamination means for valuing, developing and managing real estate, including environmental site assessments and brownfield regulation.
l2: Assembling specialist team members to advise on contaminated land assessment and remediation, undertaking Phase I environmental site assessments, advising clients accordingly, and understanding how contaminated land law and regulations apply to projects.
l3: Lead phased contaminated land assessments: appraise remediation options, supervise site investigations, interpret laboratory results, negotiate with clients and regulators, and give reasoned advice on remedial treatment.
l4: Writes or reviews site assessment standards (CSA Z768, ASTM E1527), advises regulators on remediation policy, or gives expert evidence on contamination liability and its effect on value.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Measurement
description: Measuring land and buildings to recognised standards (IPMS, ANSI/BOMA), the limits of each method and instrument, accuracy and sources of error.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of measurement principles, standards and their limits in your field, such as BOMA and IPMS standards, data capture methods and common sources of error.
l2: Measure property using suitable basic or advanced instruments, apply the correct measurement standard, and present the resulting areas and data clearly.
l3: Evaluate, manage, analyze and present measurement or spatial data, showing a command of accuracy, precision and where errors arise.
l4: Sits on a measurement standards committee (IPMS, BOMA) or is appointed by landlords and tenants to settle area measurement disputes.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Planning and development management
description: The land-use planning system: official plans and zoning, development applications and approvals, appeals to tribunals such as the Ontario Land Tribunal, and the stakeholders in planning decisions.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the development approvals system, planning application processes, and the role of key stakeholders in planning decisions.
l2: Apply knowledge to support planning applications, prepare supporting documentation, and respond to consultation processes and planning conditions.
l3: Provide strategic planning advice, lead complex applications, negotiate with planning authorities, and represent clients at tribunal hearings such as the Ontario Land Tribunal.
l4: Gives expert planning evidence in precedent-setting tribunal cases, drafts municipal or provincial planning policy, or is consulted by other firms on complex approvals.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11)

name: Risk management
description: Identifying, analysing, allocating and managing the risks in your area of practice, with risk registers, qualitative and quantitative analysis and frameworks such as ISO 31000.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of what risk is, the risks typical of your business or field, and the tools used to identify, assess and manage them, such as risk registers and quantification models.
l2: Carry out risk assessments that weigh all relevant factors, using recognized methods to measure risk, and take part in risk workshops and the reports that follow.
l3: Provide strategic advice on risk management frameworks, lead complex risk analysis, guide risk allocation strategies, and build organizational risk management capability.
l4: Designs risk frameworks adopted beyond their own team (ISO 31000-based registers, Monte Carlo cost and schedule risk analysis) and is consulted on risk in their sector.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Works progress and quality management
description: Inspecting, recording and reporting on the progress and quality of building works against the programme and specification, and managing them as contract administrator or payment certifier through to completion.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how construction progress and quality are inspected on site and recorded against the schedule and the contract's quality requirements.
l2: Apply works progress and quality management skills in practical work situations.
l3: Provide expert advice on works progress and quality management strategies to clients and project teams.
l4: Sets quality management systems for major programmes (inspection and test plans, ISO 9001 procedures), or gives expert evidence on progress, workmanship or completion disputes.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Contract administration
description: Running a construction contract day to day: payments, variations, notices, document control, meetings and reporting.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of construction contract terms and requirements, whether contractual, legislative or statutory, including standard forms such as CCDC and AIA documents and the role of the contract administrator.
l2: Apply knowledge to practical contract administration activities including issuing instructions, managing payments, dealing with variations, and certifying works.
l3: Advise on the procedures needed to administer a construction contract well, including document control, meetings, reporting, time extensions and claims, and the parties' rights and obligations.
l4: Writes contract administration procedures others use, or acts as expert or adjudicator on certification, payment and notice disputes, such as under the prompt payment and adjudication rules of Ontario's Construction Act.
source: L1-L2: RICS-APC-prep; L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Design and specification
description: The design process, design documentation and specifications (for example CSI MasterFormat), and the codes and regulations that govern design.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the design process, the scope and content of design documentation, specification formats, and the regulatory framework governing design work.
l2: Prepare designs and specifications from outline to detail levels, apply design standards and regulations, coordinate design team inputs, and manage the design development process through the design phases (schematic design, design development, construction documents).
l3: Lead the design process from inception to completion, provide strategic advice on complex design decisions, manage multi-disciplinary design teams, resolve design conflicts, and advise clients on design quality, buildability, sustainability, and value optimization.
l4: Writes master specifications or design standards others adopt (owner design guidelines, specification sections), or is engaged to review other teams' designs on major projects.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11)

name: Commercial management
description: Commercial management of construction works: procuring and negotiating terms with suppliers and subcontractors, valuing work, cash flow, change orders and claims, and final accounts.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the different elements involved in commercial management, including procuring and negotiating suitable terms for the engagement of suppliers and service providers.
l2: Apply knowledge to procure suppliers and service providers, negotiate commercial terms, manage contracts, monitor performance, and manage variations and changes.
l3: Provide strategic commercial advice, develop procurement and commercial strategies, negotiate complex arrangements, advise on contract disputes and claims, and optimize commercial outcomes.
l4: Prices and negotiates the most contested final accounts and claims for parties beyond their own firm, or gives expert evidence on the value of change orders and delay claims.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph

name: Contract practice
description: The forms of construction contract (CCDC, AIA, ConsensusDocs, FIDIC and others), their selection, warranties and the obligations they create.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the forms of contract used in construction or your line of business, such as CCDC and AIA standard forms, and of bonds, warranties and insurance.
l2: Apply your knowledge of standard contract forms at the project level, comparing key provisions and explaining what each form requires of, and means for, the parties.
l3: Give reasoned advice and present reports on choosing the form of contract, warranties and bonds that suit a procurement route, and on the right contractual procedure at each stage of a project.
l4: Drafts or amends standard forms (CCDC, AIA or ConsensusDocs committees) or gives expert evidence on contract interpretation in construction disputes.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Design economics and cost planning
description: How design decisions affect costs over the whole life of a building, and using elemental cost plans (UniFormat, for example) to keep a design within budget.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of what drives a building's design economics across its whole life, and how cost planning keeps finances under control through design development by systematic measurement, data analysis and cost forecasting.
l2: Produce Class D to A estimates and UniFormat elemental cost plans through design stages, conduct life cycle costing analysis, participate in value engineering exercises, apply benchmarking techniques, and prepare cost reports for clients and design teams.
l3: Lead cost planning strategy, provide strategic advice on cost/quality/time/buildability balance, evaluate and advise on design efficiency and value optimization, lead value management and value engineering exercises, advise on whole-life value and sustainability cost implications, and guide design teams to achieve client budgets through informed decision-making.
l4: Publishes cost benchmarks or cost-planning methods others use (elemental cost data, for example), or reviews cost plans for other organisations' major projects.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Development/project briefs
description: Preparing development and project briefs: client requirements, scope, constraints, stakeholders and change control.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of what goes into a development or project brief: the client's requirements, project definition and constraints, stakeholder roles and the team's terms of reference.
l2: Apply knowledge to practical briefing tasks including requirements capture, business case preparation, and project definition.
l3: Provide strategic advice on brief development, scope management, stakeholder engagement, and change control for complex projects.
l4: Writes briefing standards or templates other organisations adopt, or is engaged by sponsors of major programmes to set or challenge the brief, its objectives and its change control.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Housing maintenance, repair and improvements
description: Maintaining, repairing and improving housing stock: the roles of owners, tenants and housing providers, funding and maintenance programmes.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the roles of owners, tenants, housing providers and municipalities in housing maintenance; funding for repairs and improvements; the building code, residential tenancy maintenance duties and municipal property standards; and planned versus reactive maintenance.
l2: Apply your knowledge to assess housing condition (building condition assessments, unit inspections), identify property-standards and health and safety hazards, prepare repair estimates and condition reports, and run maintenance programmes and contractors.
l3: Provide reasoned advice on maintenance strategy and capital priorities for housing portfolios, repair versus replacement on whole-life cost, compliance with property standards and tenancy obligations, and funding of improvement programmes.
l4: Sets capital repair and maintenance policy for large housing providers (building condition assessments, capital plans), or advises governments on housing repair standards and funding.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L2; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11)

name: Maintenance management
description: The maintenance needs of buildings and structures: planned, preventive and reactive maintenance, life-cycle planning, maintenance records and systems, and budgets.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how buildings, structures and other real estate are maintained, including planned, preventive and reactive maintenance, inspections, budgeting and owners' and occupants' responsibilities.
l2: Keep maintenance records current and use them to set and carry out operational maintenance policies, identifying needs, ordering work and confirming it is completed satisfactorily.
l3: Provide strategic advice on maintenance policy, implement lifecycle planning, and advise on cost-benefit of different maintenance approaches.
l4: Sets maintenance and life-cycle strategy for large portfolios (reserve fund studies, computerised maintenance management systems), or writes planned-maintenance guidance others adopt.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Insurance
description: Insurance principles and practice in your area: types of cover, insurable (replacement cost) valuations, claims, and transferring risk through insurance.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of insurance principles and practice in your field, including property and liability coverage, how policies are placed and regulated, and the main terms and factors that affect them.
l2: Apply knowledge to practical insurance matters including developing specialist knowledge, compiling insurance claim data, and preparing insurable replacement cost valuations.
l3: Provide reasoned advice on complex insurance matters, including strategic recommendations on insurance requirements, handling complex claims, and advising on risk mitigation through insurance.
l4: Acts as appraisal umpire or expert in insurance disputes (insurable value, business interruption), or sets replacement-cost valuation methods that insurers and brokers adopt.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Landlord and tenant
description: The law and practice of commercial and residential tenancies under provincial or state law: lease terms, rent reviews and renewals, repairs, assignment, and the remedies available to each party.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of landlord and tenant law and practice, including the statutory and common-law framework, the form and content of leases, and market conditions that bear on them.
l2: Apply landlord and tenant law and practice by reading and interpreting leases, preparing and responding to notices, and negotiating solutions to issues between owners and occupants.
l3: Give reasoned advice and present reports on landlord and tenant matters, such as renewals, rent reviews, defaults and lease strategy, and help resolve disputes through negotiation, mediation or arbitration.
l4: Acts as arbitrator or independent expert in lease disputes (rent resets, renewals, repair obligations), or drafts lease precedents and practice guidance used across the market.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Procurement and tendering
description: The main procurement routes (design-bid-build, design-build, construction management, public-private partnerships) and the tendering and negotiation processes used to appoint consultants and contractors.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the main procurement routes, such as design-bid-build, design-build and construction management, and of how tendering and negotiation work, including prequalification and selection criteria.
l2: Implement the procurement routes chosen for your projects and carry out the related tendering and negotiation, including prequalification, tender documents and bid evaluation.
l3: Give reasoned advice on which procurement route suits a project, manage the tendering and negotiation process, and report on the outcome with a recommendation for award.
l4: Designs procurement strategies or policies for public bodies or major programmes (alternative financing and procurement, P3 or integrated project delivery) that others adopt.
source: L1: RICS-APC-prep; L2-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Project finance
description: Controlling and reporting costs during a project within its legal and contractual constraints so it stays within budget; on the Infrastructure pathway, also the funding sources and forms of finance for infrastructure.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how costs are kept under control during a project, the legal and contractual limits on doing so, and how schedule and quality affect cost; on the Infrastructure pathway, also the funding sources and forms of investment finance for infrastructure.
l2: Apply knowledge to practical project financial management including cost reporting, forecasting, and analysis of funding options.
l3: Provide strategic advice on project financing, budget management, and financial risk management.
l4: Sets cost control and reporting standards for major programmes (forecast final cost, contingency drawdown, earned value) and advises sponsors or lenders on project cost and funding risk.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Quantification and costing
description: Quantifying and costing construction works as the basis for managing contract finances: takeoff to a standard method of measurement, estimating, and pricing documents such as bills of quantities or schedules of values.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how construction work is quantified and costed as the basis for managing contract finances, including standard methods of measurement.
l2: Quantify and cost construction work at each project stage, using suitable methods of measurement and cost analysis, and produce pricing documents.
l3: Provide professional advice on quantification and costing methodologies, select appropriate pricing document formats for different procurement routes, take responsibility for measurement accuracy, negotiate and agree valuations, and resolve measurement disputes.
l4: Writes or maintains measurement and costing standards (ICMS, NRM or CSI-based estimating guides), or gives expert evidence on the quantum of construction work.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Valuation
description: Valuing real estate for its many purposes, using the right methods and bases of value under RICS Valuation Global Standards (Red Book), USPAP or CUSPAP and local law.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of valuation principles, methodologies, RICS Valuation Standards (Red Book), bases of value, and property types
l2: Apply valuation methodology to conduct valuations of different property types for various purposes, comply with Red Book requirements, prepare valuation reports
l3: Provide expert valuation advice on complex properties, advise on valuation approach and methodology, handle specialist valuations, expert witness work, strategic valuation advisory
l4: Writes or reviews valuation standards or guidance (IVS, USPAP, CUSPAP, RICS), reviews other valuers' work as an appointed review appraiser, or trains and assesses valuers as an AIC or APC assessor.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph

name: Auctioneering
description: Selling property by auction: the legal obligations, preparation, conduct of the sale and the alternatives to auction.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how auctions work and the legal duties involved, including preparation and the procedures before and on the day of sale.
l2: Demonstrate practical application of auctioneering principles, including compiling information for property to be sold at auction, assisting in catalogue preparation, dealing with queries and issues before and after auction, and producing market appraisals for reserve and guide prices.
l3: Demonstrate the ability to provide reasoned advice on the suitability of sale by auction versus other disposal methods, attend auctions and sell lots as the auctioneer, be involved with sales by auction from start to completion, and provide strategic advice on marketing approach and reserve prices.
l4: Conducts high-profile or complex auctions for other firms' clients, and writes conditions of sale or auction guidance adopted beyond their firm.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Capital taxation
description: Capital taxes on real estate and other assets (capital gains, deemed disposition at death, US estate and gift tax, land transfer taxes) and the valuations that support them.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how capital taxes apply to real estate, equipment and other assets in your jurisdiction, such as capital gains tax, and of the valuation bases they require.
l2: Apply knowledge of capital taxation provisions to practical work situations involving property and asset transactions.
l3: Provide reasoned professional advice on capital taxation matters, including strategic tax planning, negotiations with authorities, and complex valuation scenarios.
l4: Settles contested capital tax valuations with the CRA or IRS and gives expert evidence before the Tax Court of Canada or US Tax Court, or writes guidance on them.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Compulsory purchase and compensation
description: Expropriation powers and procedures (eminent domain in the US) under statutes such as Ontario's Expropriations Act, and the compensation owed for market value, injurious affection and disturbance.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of expropriation (eminent domain): the powers and procedures of governments and other authorities to take interests in land, the principles of compensation, and the rights of owners, occupants and affected third parties.
l2: Apply the principles of compulsory purchase and compensation. Calculate and negotiate compensation claims. Represent clients in negotiations with expropriating authorities or claimants. Prepare compensation assessments and supporting evidence.
l3: Provide evidence of reasoned advice on complex compulsory purchase matters. Develop strategic approaches to major compensation claims. Quantify complex claims including severance, injurious affection, and disturbance. Represent clients in tribunals and provide expert witness evidence.
l4: Leads precedent-setting expropriation claims whose decisions are cited, advises governments on acquisition and compensation policy, or writes guidance others in the field use.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Corporate recovery and insolvency
description: The surveyor's role in insolvency and restructuring (receivership, bankruptcy, CCAA or Chapter 11 proceedings): valuing, managing and disposing of property assets for receivers, trustees and lenders.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the real estate professional's role in restructuring and insolvency, such as receivership and bankruptcy proceedings, including creditors' rights and remedies and types of security.
l2: Apply your knowledge to insolvency work: identify the appointment (receivership, bankruptcy, CCAA or Chapter 11), separate encumbered, unencumbered and third-party assets, prepare asset schedules from title, and report to trustees, receivers and lenders.
l3: Leading insolvency valuations from inception to completion. Implementing and adapting valuation strategy. Providing valuation reports detailing different asset categories. Advisory reports using appropriate bases of value.
l4: Acts for receivers, trustees or lenders on major insolvency mandates, and sets property valuation and sale-process practice that others in insolvency work follow.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Development appraisals
description: Appraising development: residual valuations, cash flows, costs, finance, risk and sensitivity, to test a scheme's viability.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the principles behind a sound development pro forma or feasibility analysis, when it is used, what it contains and what its results are most sensitive to.
l2: Gather and analyze the data needed for development feasibility analysis, prepare pro formas using suitable techniques and software, test sensitivities, and identify possible sources of development financing.
l3: Interpret development feasibility analyses and give reasoned advice on acquisition, disposition, risk and financing, and on further opportunities they reveal.
l4: Builds or reviews development appraisal models others rely on (for lenders, or municipalities testing viability), or gives expert evidence on development value.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Indirect investment vehicles
description: Indirect real estate investment: REITs, limited partnerships, private funds and other vehicles, their structures, tax treatment, governance and how they are funded.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of indirect real estate investment, including the structures and instruments used to own and finance property, such as REITs, funds, partnerships, derivatives and debt.
l2: Apply knowledge to review and analyze indirect investment vehicle structures, understanding investment implications and comparative advantages.
l3: Provide strategic advice on indirect investment vehicles including establishment, management, and selection for client portfolios.
l4: Structures REITs, limited partnerships or funds for institutions, or contributes to industry standards and reporting (REALPAC, Nareit, NCREIF PREA Reporting Standards).
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Investment management (including fund and portfolio management)
description: Investing in property at asset, fund and portfolio level: strategy, performance measurement, risk and return.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how property works as a financial investment: the components of return, valuation theory, portfolio management principles and the regulation of investment managers.
l2: Apply knowledge to assist in asset management activities and demonstrate understanding of how they fit into portfolio strategic performance plans.
l3: Provide strategic investment advice at portfolio and asset level, including independent generation and implementation of strategic advice.
l4: Sets strategy for major real estate funds or pension programmes outside their own firm, or contributes to industry performance standards (NCREIF PREA, REALPAC, GIPS).
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Leasing/letting
description: Leasing and letting property: marketing, terms, negotiation and completion, the types of interest offered and the economics of the leasing market.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how different property types are leased, or space is acquired for a tenant, the kinds of interests brought to market, the economics of the leasing market and the legal framework that applies.
l2: Apply the principles of leasing and letting to market properties effectively, manage the letting process, and advise clients on rental strategy.
l3: Provide strategic advice on complex leasing and letting matters, handle unusual situations, and provide reasoned recommendations on rental strategy and market dynamics.
l4: Advises on landmark leasing transactions for others (headquarters, anchor or portfolio deals), or contributes to standard lease forms and leasing guidance used across the market.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Loan security valuation
description: Valuations for secured lending: the lending market, lender instructions and regulatory appraisal rules (the US Interagency Appraisal and Evaluation Guidelines, Canadian lender policies), valuation standards and reporting on security and risk.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of real estate lending markets and how valuations support them, including debt sources, valuation standards (Red Book, USPAP or CUSPAP), negligence case law, conflicts of interest and risk management in lending decisions.
l2: Carry out valuations for loan security purposes using suitable techniques, applying the governing valuation standards, meeting lenders' specific requirements and researching the factors that affect lending risk.
l3: Give complex, reasoned valuation advice to lenders in compliant reports, covering the property's strengths and weaknesses, loan terms, expected investment performance and wider market influences.
l4: Sets lender valuation panels, instructions or review standards, or gives expert evidence in valuation negligence claims brought by lenders.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Local taxation/assessment
description: Property tax at the municipal level: how assessors (MPAC in Ontario, US county assessors) value property, the basis of assessment, and reconsideration requests and appeals to bodies such as the Assessment Review Board.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how real estate, equipment and other property is taxed at the municipal or local level, including property tax assessment, the governing statutes and case law, and the valuation methods used.
l2: Apply knowledge of local taxation provisions to practical property assessment work.
l3: Provide expert professional advice on local taxation matters, including complex property assessments, strategic appeals, and tribunal representation.
l4: Leads precedent-setting assessment appeals whose decisions are cited, or advises assessment agencies, municipalities or legislators on assessment methods and policy.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Property finance and funding
description: The range of finance available for property, how it is sourced and structured, and how it can make a project or acquisition viable.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the range of finance available for property investment and development, how it is sourced, and how it affects returns.
l2: Apply your knowledge to identify suitable sources of finance for a project, the factors that affect obtaining it, and the terms for securing it for different purposes.
l3: Give reasoned advice on making a financing structure as viable as possible, showing how property factors affect value and financing and how financing conditions affect the property market, including multi-tiered capital stacks.
l4: Structures complex financings for others (construction, mezzanine, CMHC-insured or CMBS loans) and is consulted by lenders or industry bodies on property finance markets.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Property management
description: Managing property for owners: the landlord and tenant relationship, lease administration, operating-cost recoveries, budgets, maintenance and reporting to owners.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of property management and the owner-occupant relationship, including the manager's role, statutory requirements and how operating cost recoveries affect landlords and tenants.
l2: Apply the principles of property management to manage the relationship between owner and occupier. Carry out relevant management activities including financial management, maintenance planning, and stakeholder consultation.
l3: Provide evidence of reasoned advice on complex property management matters. Prepare and present reports with strategic recommendations. Handle disputes and advise on available options to protect client interests.
l4: Writes property management standards adopted across large portfolios or by industry bodies (operating-cost recovery, reporting, tenant service), and is consulted on complex management disputes.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Purchase and sale
description: Buying and selling property for clients: methods of sale, marketing, due diligence, negotiation and completion.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how different property types are sold, or acquired for a client, the interests that may be offered, methods of sale, the economics of the transaction market and the legal framework.
l2: Apply knowledge and understanding to undertake the sale or purchase of property interests. Carry out due diligence, prepare documentation, negotiate terms, and manage transactions through to completion.
l3: Provide evidence of reasoned advice on complex purchase and sale transactions. Develop and implement marketing and acquisition strategies. Handle complex negotiations and provide strategic advice on pricing, structuring, and risk.
l4: Advises on landmark acquisitions and disposals for others (portfolio sales, sale-leasebacks), and writes disposal or due-diligence processes adopted beyond their firm.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Strategic real estate consultancy
description: Advising on real estate as a business resource: aligning property with corporate or investment strategy, using market and portfolio analysis.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how real estate fits into a business, its structure, objectives and performance, and of the real estate professional's role as a strategic advisor.
l2: Apply knowledge and understanding to research organisational background, prepare and analyse relevant data, undertake option appraisals for real estate strategies, use different consultancy intervention styles, and use knowledge to find strategic solutions.
l3: Provide strategic advice and recommendations to clients, make presentations to clients, and present data to support recommendations. Demonstrate depth of knowledge in strategic real estate consultancy.
l4: Advises boards or governments on real estate strategy (portfolio rationalisation, sale-leaseback, footprint), and publishes or teaches strategic methods others adopt.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Business alignment
description: How a business's core drivers affect its property needs, and how property and facilities in turn affect the business.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how an organization's core business drivers shape its real estate needs, and how real estate in turn affects the business.
l2: Demonstrate practical application of business alignment principles through analysis, collaboration, and implementation.
l3: Provide strategic advice on how real estate/FM strategy contributes to business planning and operational performance, with data-driven recommendations to senior stakeholders.
l4: Advises executives of other organisations on aligning real estate and facilities with corporate strategy, and publishes or teaches the methods.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Business case
description: Preparing and presenting business cases for real estate decisions: options, costs, benefits, risks and recommendation.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of what a business case is and how it is used in corporate real estate, including its structure, the financial analysis behind it and how decisions are made.
l2: Prepare a business case in practice: gather the data, engage stakeholders and set out the financial impact of a real estate decision.
l3: Advise on preparing and presenting business cases for different purposes, offering alternative options, showing their effect on key business measures and giving a clear recommendation.
l4: Sets business case methods for an organisation or public body (options appraisal with NPV and whole-life cost) and reviews others' business cases for major real estate investments.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Change management
description: Managing change in real estate and workplace settings: planning, communication, stakeholder engagement and implementation.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of change management as it applies to real estate: what drives change, how outcomes and plans are decided, and the models, tools and option-appraisal techniques used.
l2: Take a practical part in change management projects, such as identifying the need for change, assessing options and impacts, and preparing communication and stakeholder engagement plans.
l3: Advise on developing and carrying out change strategies, setting out costs, benefits and alternatives, presenting recommendations to stakeholders and securing approval to proceed.
l4: Leads organisation-wide real estate or workplace change (relocations, hybrid-work transitions) and is engaged by other organisations to design or rescue change programmes.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Performance management
description: Measuring and managing the performance of real estate and facilities services: KPIs, benchmarking and service levels.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how performance is managed and measured, including types of performance data, measurement techniques, and how KPIs and service level agreements align with stakeholder goals.
l2: Apply performance management in a business setting by collecting benchmarking data, developing and using KPIs, and applying methods such as a balanced scorecard to improve results.
l3: Give reasoned advice on what an organization needs from performance management, interpret benchmarks and KPIs to recommend action, and show that you track performance metrics across corporate real estate services.
l4: Designs facilities or real estate performance frameworks adopted beyond their organisation (KPI sets, IFMA or BOMA benchmarking), and advises others on service levels.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Programming and planning
description: Planning and programming projects: schedules, critical path, monitoring progress and correcting delays.
l1: Describe how project schedules and budgets are monitored, including techniques such as Gantt charts and critical path analysis, and demonstrate knowledge of the types of schedules and scheduling software used on projects.
l2: Apply programming and planning techniques in practice, including developing programmes, monitoring progress, analyzing delays, and reporting on schedule performance.
l3: Provide strategic advice on programming strategies, produce comprehensive programmes showing critical path, advise on corrective measures for delays, and conduct sophisticated programme analysis including acceleration and recovery.
l4: Sets scheduling standards for major programmes (critical path baselines, delay analysis to AACE 29R-03) or gives expert evidence on delay and disruption.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Supplier management
description: Managing suppliers so that the scope and value of the service meet organisational requirements: selection, contracts and performance.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how vendors and service providers are managed through a structured process, using contracts, service level agreements, KPIs and performance monitoring, so that scope and value meet the organization's needs.
l2: Manage vendors using your organization's established process, for example through performance review meetings, audits, budgeting and change orders, so that the service delivered meets its required scope and value.
l3: Show that you tailor how a vendor or group of vendors is managed to the size of the service and the risk of its failure, using customer feedback, partnership and innovation in the supply chain.
l4: Designs supplier management frameworks for an organisation or sector (category strategies, scorecards, contract KPIs) and advises others on strategic sourcing of services.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Workspace strategy
description: How workspace strategy supports a business: space planning, workplace models, utilisation and occupier needs.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of why workplace strategy matters to a business, including types of work environment, how their efficiency and effectiveness are measured, and how strategy choices affect the organization.
l2: Use workplace strategy in practice to improve business performance, evaluating space by cost, utilization studies and occupant feedback, and tracking KPIs for a strategy's implementation.
l3: Give reasoned advice on workplace strategies that improve business performance, aligning the work environment with business processes and occupant needs and presenting the case for change to stakeholders.
l4: Advises major occupiers on workplace strategy (activity-based working, utilisation studies, hybrid models) and publishes or speaks on workplace research that others cite.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Environmental management
description: Environmental management concepts, processes and systems, such as ISO 14001, and how they apply to projects and organisations.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of environmental management concepts, processes and systems, such as ISO 14001, compliance obligations, sustainability principles and site remediation.
l2: Apply environmental and land management concepts, processes and systems in practice, including monitoring, reporting and interpreting legislation and permits to achieve compliance.
l3: Provide strategic environmental management advice, lead environmental management processes, and ensure compliance with sustainability principles.
l4: Designs environmental management systems for organisations or a sector (ISO 14001 implementation and certification audits) or contributes to EMS standards and guidance.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Consultancy services
description: Procuring and delivering advisory and strategic consultancy services: scoping, method, analysis, reporting and client value.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how advisory and strategic consulting services are procured and delivered, including engagement agreements, confidentiality, common risks and KPIs.
l2: Deliver consulting services in practice: prepare service plans and client briefs, report to clients, and manage resources and client expectations.
l3: Give reasoned strategic advice to clients, preparing and presenting consulting reports with supporting analysis and recommendations.
l4: Retained by boards, governments or other consultancies for specialist advice, with reports or methods that others in the field cite or adopt.
source: L1: RICS-APC-prep; L2-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Environmental assessments
description: Environmental assessment concepts and processes, the legal duties behind them (Canada's Impact Assessment Act, provincial environmental assessment acts, NEPA in the US), and reporting on environmental effects.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of environmental assessment concepts, processes and systems, including environmental impact assessment, when it is required, and the duties set by statutes, regulations and codes of practice.
l2: Apply your understanding of environmental assessment and its compliance requirements in practice, including carrying out or managing the preparation of an assessment.
l3: Give reasoned advice on the need for, scope of and findings from environmental assessments, and prepare the resulting reports and statements.
l4: Leads major assessments under federal, provincial or state law (federal impact assessments, provincial environmental assessments, NEPA environmental impact statements), or advises regulators on assessment practice.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Environmental audit (and monitoring)
description: Environmental auditing and monitoring: audit scope and methods (ISO 14001 and ISO 19011), compliance audits, reporting nonconformities and following up corrective actions.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of environmental auditing concepts, processes and systems, such as ISO 14001 and ISO 19011, and how audits support environmental monitoring and compliance.
l2: Carrying out environmental audit and reporting to set requirements, understanding scope and methods for environmental audit, identifying specialisms and specialists required, and reporting nonconformities.
l3: Presenting and proposing actions following findings of environmental audit, advising clients on needs of environmental audit, negotiating and liaising with clients and regulators on findings and actions, and managing nonconformities including corrective and preventative actions.
l4: Sets environmental audit programmes for organisations or a sector (ISO 14001 and ISO 19011, regulatory compliance audits) and is the lead auditor others rely on.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Environmental science and processes
description: The environmental sciences, especially how human activity affects the natural and built environment, and interpreting specialist reports.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of environmental science, covering ecology, soil, water and air, and how human activity affects the natural and built environment and human health.
l2: Interpret specialist environmental reports and specifications to advise on present and future environmental implications, and identify the specialists a site needs.
l3: Advise on need, scope and methods of environmental sciences; review and interpret specialist reports; advise on implications for future actions; specify requirements for assessments by specialists; undertake specialist assessments and modelling; liaise with clients, regulators and third parties; advise on strategy for environmental science aspects.
l4: Peer-reviews other specialists' environmental reports for regulators or tribunals, or publishes applied environmental science on land and property.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Management of the natural environment and landscape
description: Nature conservation and landscape in real estate, business and development: habitats, protected areas, and landscape value.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of why nature conservation and landscape matter in real estate, business management and development, including protected-area designations, conservation programs and the legislation and agencies behind them.
l2: Apply your knowledge of nature conservation and landscape when managing or developing real estate, for example on habitat programs, land-use approvals, and mapping and survey requirements.
l3: Give reasoned advice, write reports and negotiate on nature conservation and landscape matters, including land use, management practice and balancing competing interests.
l4: Advises governments or conservation bodies on habitat and landscape policy (conservation easements, species-at-risk habitat), and shapes practice beyond their own projects.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Energy and renewable resources
description: Energy and renewable energy resources and facilities (wind, solar, hydro, storage, transmission): their economics, technical viability, land agreements, inspection and monitoring.
l1: Show broad familiarity with energy and renewable energy resources and technologies, such as solar, wind and hydro, and with how energy facilities are inspected.
l2: Show experience assessing the economic and technical viability of energy and renewable energy facilities and monitoring their performance, including agreements, royalties, incentives and cash flow analysis.
l3: Provide reasoned advice to clients across a wide range of energy and renewable resources services, taking responsibility for formal reports, with a thorough knowledge of the sector.
l4: Advises on major energy assets or programmes (wind, solar, storage and transmission land agreements and valuation) and is consulted by regulators or industry bodies on energy land policy.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Environmental analysis
description: Environmental laboratory practice: accreditation (ISO/IEC 17025, CALA in Canada, TNI in the US), setting an analytical scope, sampling, and interpreting laboratory results.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of good practice in environmental laboratories, including accreditation, analytical techniques, and how samples are collected, contained and prepared.
