l2: Set a suitable scope of laboratory analysis for a site, taking into account its current and past uses, environmental setting and intended use.
l3: Interpret laboratory results against suitable criteria and recommend any further analysis or action, such as identifying contaminants of concern and ways to mitigate them.
l4: Sets laboratory or sampling standards (ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation, CALA or TNI programmes) and reviews other practitioners' analytical results as an expert.

name: Forestry and woodland management
description: Managing forests and woodland: silviculture, species, timber production, amenity and the economics of woodland systems.
l1: Describe the main commercial and amenity tree species, how to identify them and their silvicultural requirements, and demonstrate knowledge of current incentive programs, timber sale options, value-added opportunities, prices and markets.
l2: Apply knowledge to woodland management: planting and establishment, grant applications, and silvicultural practice including harvesting and marketing.
l3: Preparing woodland management plans, providing strategic advice to clients, understanding economics and financial implications of various forest and woodland systems, preparing and submitting grant scheme applications, calculating timber yields, carrying out valuations of trees and stands, and drawing up thinning and harvest programmes.
l4: Advises governments, Indigenous communities or large landowners on forest management plans and certification (FSC, SFI), and shapes woodland practice beyond their own estates.

name: GIS
description: Geographic information science and systems: GIS software, data structures, spatial analysis and presenting spatial information.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of geographic information science and systems: industry-standard GIS software, how spatial data is typed and structured and what it is used for, how it is captured, and how results are output.
l2: Apply GIS knowledge in practical projects, demonstrating ability to assess data quality, specify capture methods, conduct spatial analysis, manage databases, and apply national and international standards.
l3: Provide professional consultancy-level advice on GIS strategy, system selection, data management, and implementation, demonstrating ability to analyze user requirements and design GIS solutions.
l4: Sets GIS strategy and spatial data standards for organisations (enterprise geodatabases, OGC standards) and is consulted by others on spatial systems.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Ground engineering and subsidence
description: Ground conditions and subsidence: site investigation, geology, foundations, and diagnosing and remedying ground movement.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the investigations, including site inspection, used to research site history and geology.
l2: Gather, analyze and interpret information from initial research, such as geological and mining records, to assess ground movement risk and treatment options.
l3: Provide expert advice on complex ground engineering and subsidence issues, including geotechnical risk assessment and remediation strategies.
l4: Gives expert evidence on subsidence and ground-movement claims, or advises others on complex ground risk (karst, old mine workings, expansive clays).
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Land use and diversification
description: How land uses, policies and diversification options affect real estate and rural businesses.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how different land uses, policies and diversification options affect real estate and businesses, including zoning, the agencies involved and basic tax considerations.
l2: Apply knowledge to prepare feasibility studies and business cases for diversification projects, understanding planning, financial and operational implications.
l3: Provide strategic advice on complex diversification projects, including valuation, financial management, and reasoned advice on land use change and diversification strategies.
l4: Advises major landowners or governments on land-use change and diversification (renewables leases, conservation, agri-tourism) and publishes or teaches practice others follow.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Management and regeneration of the built environment
description: Sustainable management and regeneration of the built environment as part of planning, renewal and community development.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of why sustainable management of the built environment matters in land-use planning and urban redevelopment, including the economic, social and environmental factors involved.
l2: Use what you know about managing the built environment sustainably in planning and redevelopment work, and show you understand the roles of the public, private and non-profit sectors.
l3: Provide expert advice on sustainable management strategies, regeneration approaches, and multi-sector partnership development for complex built environment projects.
l4: Advises governments on renewal programmes (community improvement plans, brownfield and tax-increment financing) and leads multi-sector partnerships that others study.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Surveying and mapping
description: The principles of surveying and mapping: accuracy, scale, data capture and presentation of spatial information.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of mapping and geographic information science principles in your field, and of how to judge whether maps, drawings, imagery and plans, on paper or digital, are accurate, current, at a suitable scale and fit for the purpose.
l2: Apply knowledge of surveying and mapping techniques in practical work situations. Demonstrate ability to plan, execute, and process surveys using modern equipment and software.
l3: Provide reasoned advice on survey methodology, design control networks, manage survey projects, and ensure fitness-for-purpose of survey deliverables. Demonstrate strategic thinking and problem-solving in complex survey applications.
l4: Sets survey and mapping specifications for major programmes (accuracy standards such as ASPRS) and advises others on survey method and fitness for purpose.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Waste management
description: Waste management law, policy and operations (landfill, recycling, treatment) and the real estate and planning issues they raise.
l1: Understanding current and emerging legislation including provincial and state waste law (for example Ontario's Environmental Protection Act and Resource Recovery and Circular Economy Act, the US RCRA and state solid-waste rules); various waste management technologies dealing with collection, recycling, treatment and disposal; estates and planning management functions; and how to inspect facilities to assess property issues.
l2: Apply your knowledge to the practical and regulatory side of waste management: inspect facilities and assess the economic and technical viability, management and monitoring of their operations.
l3: Carrying out detailed valuations and financial appraisals, preparing reports to clients in support of development opportunities, designing and/or project managing planning and/or permit applications or waste treatment/disposal tenders, managing property interests including purchase and sale of waste assets, and identifying and evaluating related business opportunities including new technologies.
l4: Advises operators and governments on waste facility siting, approvals and policy (extended producer responsibility, landfill capacity), and is consulted beyond their own firm.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11)

name: Asset management
description: Managing physical assets to meet organisational objectives: asset strategy, life-cycle costs, performance and standards such as ISO 55000.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of why and how assets are managed: the aims, strategies and processes, including asset records, maintenance versus replacement decisions and information systems.
l2: Demonstrate practical application of asset management principles in FM operations, including developing asset registers, implementing maintenance strategies, and making repair vs. replacement decisions.
l3: Provide strategic advice on asset management approaches aligned with organizational objectives, implementing recognized standards, and balancing lifecycle costs against operational requirements.
l4: Sets ISO 55001-based asset management systems for organisations (for example municipal asset management plans under Ontario Regulation 588/17) and contributes to standards or guidance.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Big data
description: Big data: its sources, processing, analytics and limits, and how it can support decisions in the built environment.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and awareness of how big data is processed, the sources available, how data changes over time, and current research issues in the field.
l2: Apply data quality and hygiene techniques and statistical modelling, analysis and visual interrogation to large datasets with suitable tools.
l3: Provide strategic advice on implementing big data analytics to create business value, including data security, governance, ethics, and visualization strategies for diverse audiences.
l4: Designs data platforms or analytics programmes that other built environment organisations adopt, or publishes methods for using big data in property decisions.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Managing projects
description: Managing projects across the whole life cycle: feasibility, planning, governance, delivery, control and close-out.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the full project life cycle, including feasibility studies, project control tools and techniques, the project manager's role, and what a project audit or closeout report must contain.
l2: Apply project management tools and techniques in practice, including preparing project execution plans, managing controls, and reporting on performance.
l3: Provide strategic advice on project execution, governance, value management, performance improvement, and project recovery for complex projects.
l4: Directs major programmes and sets project governance others follow (stage gates, PMO standards), or reviews troubled projects for sponsors.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Smart cities and intelligent buildings
description: Smart cities and intelligent buildings: sensor data from buildings, people and infrastructure, and how it is processed and used.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge of the data that building, personal and infrastructure sensors can collect and how it is processed to support managing and visualizing the built environment.
l2: Collect, store and manage spatial sensor data in practice, showing how you achieve data quality, clean data and data security.
l3: Advise on use cases for capturing and storing sensor data in structures that can be analyzed by conventional and visual methods, including the business case and the risks.
l4: Shapes smart building or city strategy for governments or major owners (sensor networks, building automation integration, data-sharing policy) and contributes to standards.

name: Stakeholder management
description: Engaging and communicating with project stakeholders, including public consultation and Indigenous engagement where it applies: identification, analysis, engagement plans and managing their interests.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the principles and techniques for engaging and communicating with project stakeholders, including how decisions are made in client organizations with several decision-makers.
l2: Apply knowledge to identify stakeholders, develop stakeholder engagement strategies, implement consultation processes, manage stakeholder relationships, and respond to stakeholder concerns.
l3: Provide strategic advice on stakeholder management, develop sophisticated engagement strategies, navigate complex multi-stakeholder environments, mediate conflicts, and influence decision-making processes.
l4: Leads engagement on contentious public projects, including Indigenous consultation, and sets engagement practice that other organisations follow.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Cadastre and land administration
description: Boundary and cadastral surveys and land registration in your jurisdiction, such as provincial land titles and registry systems, US deed recording, and the US Public Land Survey System.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how boundary or cadastral surveys are carried out in the field and the office in your jurisdiction, of legal and physical boundaries with examples, and of land administration principles and land registration systems.
l2: Apply knowledge to practical cadastral work including applying land registration principles, preparing evidence for legal processes, and practicing with independence from client.
l3: Provide reasoned advice on complex cadastral matters, act as expert witness, and advise on dispute resolution.
l4: Sits on a land surveying regulator or standards body (a provincial association of land surveyors, for example), advises on land registration reform, or is cited as the authority on boundary evidence.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Engineering surveying
description: Engineering surveying: instruments (total stations, GNSS, laser scanners), survey control, setting out, and measuring and monitoring construction works.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of engineering survey principles, instrumentation, setting-out techniques, and construction measurement.
l2: Apply engineering survey knowledge in practical projects, demonstrating instrumentation selection, accuracy management, working within a survey team, and site safety implementation.
l3: Provide professional advice on engineering surveys, define specifications and tolerances, manage large-scale survey operations, and contribute to project management decision-making.
l4: Sets survey control and setting-out specifications for major projects (tunnels, bridges, transit) and advises others on monitoring and deformation surveys.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11)

name: Geodesy
description: Geodesy: reference frames and datums (NAD83(CSRS), NAD83(2011), CGVD2013, NAVD 88), geoid models, map projections, coordinate transformations and GNSS positioning.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of geodesy principles: GNSS, geodetic reference systems at global, regional and national levels (such as NAD83 and NAVD88), geoids, datums and map projections.
l2: Put geodesy into practice: plan and specify surveys and the instruments they need, allow for sources of error and whether data is fit for its purpose, work in industry-standard software, and carry out network adjustments or transformations.
l3: Give reasoned advice on advanced geodetic practice and survey planning, use advanced software for adjustment and analysis, and advise on client specifications and deliverables.
l4: Contributes to geodetic reference frameworks or their adoption (datum modernisation, for example) and advises others on high-precision positioning and transformations.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Hydrographic surveying
description: Hydrographic surveying: measuring and charting water bodies and the seabed (echo sounding, tides, positioning) to standards such as IHO S-44, and the limits of each method.
l1: Demonstrate working knowledge and understanding of hydrographic surveying, its principles and limits, and how measurements are taken in the marine environment.
l2: Apply hydrographic surveying knowledge to plan and execute marine surveys, ensuring correct calibration and compliance with technical standards.
l3: Provide expert strategic advice on hydrographic survey methodology, manage complex marine survey operations, and advise on technical, contractual, and policy matters.
l4: Sets hydrographic survey specifications (IHO S-44 orders) for major programmes and advises others on charting or marine construction surveys.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Remote sensing and photogrammetry
description: Remote sensing and photogrammetry: aerial, satellite and drone imagery and LiDAR, data processing and accuracy.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of remote sensing and photogrammetry, from aerial, satellite and terrestrial platforms including LiDAR: scale, how sensors and cameras work, and how data is captured.
l2: Apply your knowledge to routine data capture and processing: plan captures, adjust and transform data, and produce outputs with standard industry software to a stated accuracy (for example the ASPRS standards).
l3: Demonstrate the ability to provide reasoned advice on tenders and contracts, compare and advise on benefits of alternative methodology, undertake project design and draft quality plans and method statements, manage projects and contracts, and produce reports with error detection and analysis.
l4: Designs major capture programmes (provincial or state LiDAR, orthoimagery) and sets accuracy specifications such as the ASPRS positional accuracy standards.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Surveying land and sea
description: Geomatics across land, sea and the built environment: survey methods, instruments, accuracy and applications.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of geomatics principles and of how its techniques are used on land, at sea and in the built environment.
l2: Apply geomatics principles and techniques to conduct land and/or sea surveys, ensuring appropriate accuracy, quality control, and fitness for purpose.
l3: Provide expert advice on survey strategies, accuracy specifications, method selection, and complex geomatics applications to clients and project teams.
l4: Sets survey strategy for multi-discipline programmes (land, hydrographic and building survey), integrating datums and accuracy, and is consulted by other organisations on geomatics.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Use of the marine environment
description: Using the marine environment: inshore and offshore resource development and conservation, and its legal and regulatory framework.
l1: Demonstrate understanding of how inshore and offshore resources are developed, used or conserved, and of the legal and environmental issues that apply.
l2: Apply those principles to planning the use of marine resources, using suitable marine data capture and analysis software or instruments.
l3: Oversee operations that use marine resources, analyze the data collected and report on it, and advise on national and international policy for managing ocean and inshore resources.
l4: Advises governments or operators on marine use and policy (offshore wind leasing, aquaculture, marine protected areas).
source: L1-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Environmental assessment
description: Environmental assessment concepts and processes, the legal duties behind them (Canada's Impact Assessment Act, provincial environmental assessment acts, NEPA in the US), and reporting on environmental effects.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of environmental assessment concepts, processes and systems, including environmental impact assessment, when it is required, and the duties set by statutes, regulations and codes of practice.
l2: Apply your understanding of environmental assessment and its compliance requirements in practice, including carrying out or managing the preparation of an assessment.
l3: Give reasoned advice on the need for, scope of and findings from environmental assessments, and prepare the resulting reports and statements.
l4: Leads major assessments under federal, provincial or state law (federal impact assessments, provincial environmental assessments, NEPA environmental impact statements), or advises regulators on assessment practice.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Engineering science and technology
description: The engineering principles of design, methodology, logistics and construction in your field of infrastructure or industry.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of design principles, construction methods and logistics in your field of practice, including design stages, constraints and coordination between disciplines.
l2: Apply knowledge in practical work situations, demonstrating ability to use design information in project context, cost planning, and facilities management.
l3: Provide professional advice on engineering solutions, construction methodologies, and technology choices, demonstrating strategic thinking and professional judgment.
l4: Advises other organisations on major engineering solutions for infrastructure or industry, and contributes to technical codes or guidance.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Cost prediction and analysis
description: Predicting and analysing the cost of assets over their life: estimating, cost benchmarks, cost data and design economics.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of what drives the cost of a design over an asset's whole life, and how benchmarking and cost plans keep a project's finances under control from inception to the decision to proceed.
l2: Manage costs through design development and the asset's life cycle, preparing estimates, cost plans and benchmark studies, and submit cost data to internal or external data collection agencies.
l3: Give strategic, reasoned advice and present reports covering cost, schedule, quality, logistics and construction method; advise on market factors and cost trends; and comment on accuracy and risk.
l4: Publishes cost benchmarks or estimating methods others use (AACE estimate classes, elemental cost databases) and reviews estimates for other organisations' major projects.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Project controls
description: Project controls: work breakdown structures, earned value, scheduling, cost control and forecasting.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of project controls tools and techniques, such as earned value management, work breakdown structures, cash flow forecasting, budgeting, cost planning, change control, and productivity and resource analysis.
l2: Interpret, analyze and report on the data that project controls produce, to support decisions that look back at what happened and forward to what will happen.
l3: Show how you advise on strategies and procedures for analyzing, forecasting and controlling project time and cost, and give expert advice on cost control strategies and financial forecasting.
l4: Sets project controls frameworks for major programmes (earned value to EIA-748, integrated cost and schedule) and advises sponsors or tribunals on control failures.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Quantification, costing and price analysis
description: Quantifying, costing and analysing the prices of works as the basis for managing project finances.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how work is quantified, costed and unit rates are analyzed, as the basis for managing a project's finances.
l2: Quantify and cost work using suitable standard methods of measurement, benchmarking and cost analysis, and apply unit-rate analysis both to past costs and to forecasts.
l3: Advise on how to analyze, forecast and control time and cost on projects; be accountable for producing and issuing pricing documents; and price or analyze them.
l4: Sets costing and price analysis standards others use, or gives expert evidence on the valuation of works and price adjustments in disputes.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Building information modelling (BIM) management
description: The technical, process and collaborative sides of building information modelling (BIM): ISO 19650, BIM execution plans, information requirements and common data environments.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of building information modeling: the technology, the processes and the collaboration it depends on, including data capture, classification systems and relevant standards.
l2: Set up and run the management processes that support BIM on projects, such as BIM execution plans, protocols, shared control and reporting procedures, and upkeep of the information model.
l3: Advise clients or senior management on BIM strategy at the corporate or project level, drawing on your experience to compare solutions and explain their contractual, commercial and technical implications.
l4: Writes BIM standards or templates adopted beyond their team (ISO 19650 guidance, the US National BIM Standard, buildingSMART Canada work), or sets an owner's BIM requirements for major programmes.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Cross cultural awareness in a global business
description: How business is done in different cultures: drivers, etiquette and assumptions, and adapting client work, teams and negotiation accordingly.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how business is done in different cultures, including the motivations, values, etiquette and assumptions found in international business and their effect on contractual relationships.
l2: Apply that knowledge across business skills such as client relations, teamwork, leadership, negotiation and communication when working with people from other cultures.
l3: Advise clients and senior leaders, with reasons, on strategies and tactics for handling cultural issues in international business, so that corporate and project performance stays effective.
l4: Advises executives of other organisations on operating across cultures (market entry, cross-border negotiation, global teams), and leads international teams that others study.
source: L1: RICS-APC-prep; L2-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Leading projects, people and teams
description: Leading and managing projects, people and teams: leadership styles, motivation, performance and team development.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the qualities and behaviors needed to lead and manage teams, including leadership styles, motivation theory and what makes a high-performing team.
l2: Apply leadership and team management skills in practical project settings, including team selection, performance management, and motivation.
l3: Provide strategic advice on team structure, lead diverse project teams, manage poor performance, and adapt leadership approach to different contexts.
l4: Leads beyond their own organisation: chairs industry bodies or committees, mentors other leaders, or builds teams that others benchmark against.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Access and rights over land
description: Acquiring access and rights over land for utilities, pipelines and other infrastructure: easements, rights-of-way, negotiation and compensation.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the legislation and framework for acquiring sites, easements and rights-of-way for power, water, pipelines, telecommunications and other third-party or temporary uses, including how such interests are valued and compensated.
l2: Apply the principles and legislation relating to access rights and rights over land. Negotiate and agree access agreements, easements, rights-of-way and licences. Advise on and survey access rights to appropriate scale and accuracy.
l3: Provide evidence of reasoned advice on complex access disputes and rights over land. Develop strategic approaches to infrastructure routing and access negotiations. Act as expert witness in access disputes. Provide valuation advice on rights and compensation.
l4: Advises utilities, regulators or governments on land rights policy for linear infrastructure (easement compensation frameworks, routing), or leads precedent cases before energy boards or expropriation tribunals.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Agriculture
description: Agriculture: crop and animal husbandry, farm operations, legislation and the economics of farm businesses.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of basic crop and animal husbandry, timings of relevant agricultural operations, legislation affecting agriculture, current economic state of agriculture, farm support systems, and principles of agriculture according to different geographical, soil and climatic conditions.
l2: Apply the principles and systems of practical farming, including crop and livestock yields, current commodity prices, production costs, farm business management, and the use and cost of farm buildings.
l3: Demonstrate the ability to provide professional farm management advice in both written and oral form, provide reasoned advice to stakeholders on management and practical application of appropriate farming methods, undertake strategic business planning for farm enterprises, and provide expert opinion on farm performance and optimization.
l4: Advises major agricultural businesses or governments on farm business and policy, and is consulted on farm valuation or tenancy matters beyond their own practice.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Economic development
description: Economic development policy at international, national, regional and local level, and its link to property and regeneration.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of what makes economic development policy sound, set against international, national, regional and local economic conditions, including strategies for attracting investment and for urban redevelopment.
l2: Apply knowledge to make appropriate use of statistical sources, select funding and grant sources, understand organizational responsibilities, and explain place marketing and investment attraction.
l3: Provide strategic advice on economic development, conduct sophisticated economic analysis (employment, census, floor space, business surveys), perform grant calculations, and advise on economic development strategies aligned with property opportunities.
l4: Advises governments or development agencies on economic strategy (investment attraction, employment lands) and evaluates programmes that others run.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Masterplanning and urban design
description: Preparing masterplans and urban design strategies: context, layout, density, public realm and delivery.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the information needed to prepare master plans and urban design strategies, including site and area context, environmental features, stakeholder consultation, and market and planning policy.
l2: Apply knowledge to contribute to site analysis, design concept development, stakeholder engagement, and preparation of masterplan documentation.
l3: Lead masterplan preparation, provide strategic design advice, navigate complex design and stakeholder challenges, and ensure masterplan delivery through planning and implementation.
l4: Leads major masterplans and writes urban design guidelines or policies that municipalities adopt.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Minerals management
description: Minerals: geology, exploration, mining methods, minerals planning and the valuation of mineral interests.
l1: Show broad familiarity with geology, with how mineral deposits are explored and sites investigated, and with mining methods at surface and underground.
l2: Apply knowledge to practical minerals management activities including advising on legal agreements, evaluating facilities, preparing planning applications, and monitoring compliance.
l3: Provide strategic advice and leadership on complex minerals management matters including designing exploitation schemes and managing minerals operations.
l4: Advises operators and governments on mineral estates, and gives expert evidence on mineral property valuation (CIMVAL Code, NI 43-101 technical reports).
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Spatial planning policy and infrastructure
description: National, provincial and state spatial planning and infrastructure systems, their legislation and key policies.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge of the land-use planning and infrastructure systems in your jurisdiction, at federal, provincial or state and municipal levels, their legislative basis, and the main policies and programs.
l2: Apply knowledge of spatial planning policy and infrastructure to contribute to plan-making, consultations, and evaluation of policy implications for development decisions.
l3: Provide strategic advice on spatial planning policy development, infrastructure delivery, and representation of stakeholder interests in plan-making and plan approval and hearing processes.
l4: Drafts or shapes provincial, state or regional planning and infrastructure policy (growth plans, infrastructure plans) and represents interests in plan-making.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Research methodologies and techniques
description: Research methods: collecting, handling, analysing and interpreting data and other material to answer a client's question.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge of how to gather and organize data and other material, familiarity with data sources, and with techniques for handling and manipulating data.
l2: Analyze and interpret data and other material effectively, using research methods and techniques suited to the question and matched to what the client needs.
l3: Apply your analysis and interpretation of research to client requirements, reporting advice grounded in detailed data and evaluating how well the methods used performed.
l4: Publishes peer-reviewed or industry research others rely on, peer-reviews others' research, or leads research programmes for professional bodies or universities.
source: L1-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); L1 adapted for the graph; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Corporate finance
description: Corporate finance: capital structure, cost of capital, financing alternatives and the valuation of companies and securities.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of corporate finance principles including capital structure theory, cost of capital, and financing alternatives.
l2: Apply your knowledge to structuring and financing corporate transactions involving real estate: model the cost of capital and support advice on capital structure options for operational and surplus real estate, within the regulatory framework.
l3: Provide strategic advice on complex corporate finance matters including acquisition structures, complex securities valuation, and optimal capital structure decisions.
l4: Advises boards of other organisations on capital structure and major transactions (fairness opinions, M&A, recapitalisations).
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11)

name: Development projects/briefs
description: Preparing development and project briefs: client requirements, scope, constraints, stakeholders and change control.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of what goes into a development or project brief: the client's requirements, project definition and constraints, stakeholder roles and the team's terms of reference.
l2: Apply knowledge to practical briefing tasks including requirements capture, business case preparation, and project definition.
l3: Provide strategic advice on brief development, scope management, stakeholder engagement, and change control for complex projects.
l4: Writes briefing standards or templates other organisations adopt, or is engaged by sponsors of major programmes to set or challenge the brief, its objectives and its change control.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Managing resources
description: Managing the effective use, allocation and cost of an organisation's resources, other than people.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the resources a business needs to operate effectively and what they cost, including budgeting, forecasting and accounting techniques.
l2: Show how, in your own work, you have used and allocated resources as effectively as possible and managed their cost, for example by setting objectives, building budgets and monitoring spending.
l3: Evaluate how resources were managed in specific business cases, for example through cost-benefit analysis, monitoring performance against budget and acting on shortfalls.
l4: Sets resource strategy for an organisation (space, technology, equipment and budget allocation) and advises others on resource allocation and cost.
source: L1-L2: RICS-APC-prep; L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15); L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Development project briefs
description: Preparing development and project briefs: client requirements, scope, constraints, stakeholders and change control.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of what goes into a development or project brief: the client's requirements, project definition and constraints, stakeholder roles and the team's terms of reference.
l2: Apply knowledge to practical briefing tasks including requirements capture, business case preparation, and project definition.
l3: Provide strategic advice on brief development, scope management, stakeholder engagement, and change control for complex projects.
l4: Writes briefing standards or templates other organisations adopt, or is engaged by sponsors of major programmes to set or challenge the brief, its objectives and its change control.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Object identification
description: Identifying art, antiques and other personal property: the object identification checklist, attribution, authentication and dating.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the checklist used to identify an object and the characteristics to observe, so that you can describe and identify it accurately using a standard method.
l2: Apply identification and authentication knowledge in practice, conducting systematic examination and research to determine authenticity, attribution, and date.
l3: Provide expert opinion on attribution, authentication, and dating; advise clients on complex identification issues; and engage scientific expertise strategically.
l4: Gives attribution and authentication opinions that institutions, insurers or courts rely on, and publishes in their field of objects.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Housing strategy and provision
description: Assessing housing need and the options for housing provision: market assessments, affordable housing and delivery models.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how housing need is assessed (housing needs assessments), tenure types (social, affordable, co-operative, market rental and ownership), funding tools (CMHC and provincial programmes, inclusionary zoning, US Low-Income Housing Tax Credits) and the roles of municipalities, non-profit providers and developers.
l2: Apply your knowledge to research housing need and market data, contribute to housing strategies and needs assessments, determine suitable house types, tenures and funding, and negotiate and consult with clients and stakeholders.
l3: Provide reasoned advice to municipalities, housing providers and developers on housing provision, tenure mix and affordability, and options for meeting identified need within policy and financial constraints.
l4: Advises governments and housing providers on housing need assessments and supply policy (affordable housing programmes, inclusionary zoning).
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L2; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11)

name: Consultancy Services
description: Procuring and delivering advisory and strategic consultancy services: scoping, method, analysis, reporting and client value.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how advisory and strategic consulting services are procured and delivered, including engagement agreements, confidentiality, common risks and KPIs.
l2: Deliver consulting services in practice: prepare service plans and client briefs, report to clients, and manage resources and client expectations.
l3: Give reasoned strategic advice to clients, preparing and presenting consulting reports with supporting analysis and recommendations.
l4: Retained by boards, governments or other consultancies for specialist advice, with reports or methods that others in the field cite or adopt.
source: L1: RICS-APC-prep; L2-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Financial modelling
description: Building and using financial models to show the risk and return of investment and development scenarios, with sensitivity analysis.
l1: Demonstrate a basic understanding of the main financial modeling tools, such as ARGUS and Excel, and how they are used to build a model showing the risk and return of a development or investment scenario.
l2: Build custom financial models from base information, with full property analysis and cash flows that reflect the specific investment or development, and run sensitivity analysis on key variables.
l3: Use financial models to give detailed, reasoned advice on how investment and development scenarios perform, running full sensitivity analysis across inputs and assumptions and separating returns to senior debt from returns to equity.
l4: Sets model standards (FAST Standard, independent model audit) or reviews others' models, or gives expert evidence on financial projections.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Commercial management (of construction works)
description: Commercial management of construction works: procuring and negotiating terms with suppliers and subcontractors, valuing work, cash flow, change orders and claims, and final accounts.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the different elements involved in commercial management, including procuring and negotiating suitable terms for the engagement of suppliers and service providers.
l2: Apply knowledge to procure suppliers and service providers, negotiate commercial terms, manage contracts, monitor performance, and manage variations and changes.
l3: Provide strategic commercial advice, develop procurement and commercial strategies, negotiate complex arrangements, advise on contract disputes and claims, and optimize commercial outcomes.
l4: Prices and negotiates the most contested final accounts and claims for parties beyond their own firm, or gives expert evidence on the value of change orders and delay claims.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph

name: Project finance (control and reporting)
description: Controlling and reporting costs during a project within its legal and contractual constraints so it stays within budget; on the Infrastructure pathway, also the funding sources and forms of finance for infrastructure.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how costs are kept under control during a project, the legal and contractual limits on doing so, and how schedule and quality affect cost; on the Infrastructure pathway, also the funding sources and forms of investment finance for infrastructure.
l2: Apply knowledge to practical project financial management including cost reporting, forecasting, and analysis of funding options.
l3: Provide strategic advice on project financing, budget management, and financial risk management.
l4: Sets cost control and reporting standards for major programmes (forecast final cost, contingency drawdown, earned value) and advises sponsors or lenders on project cost and funding risk.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Quantification and costing (of construction works)
description: Quantifying and costing construction works as the basis for managing contract finances: takeoff to a standard method of measurement, estimating, and pricing documents such as bills of quantities or schedules of values.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how construction work is quantified and costed as the basis for managing contract finances, including standard methods of measurement.
l2: Quantify and cost construction work at each project stage, using suitable methods of measurement and cost analysis, and produce pricing documents.
l3: Provide professional advice on quantification and costing methodologies, select appropriate pricing document formats for different procurement routes, take responsibility for measurement accuracy, negotiate and agree valuations, and resolve measurement disputes.
l4: Writes or maintains measurement and costing standards (ICMS, NRM or CSI-based estimating guides), or gives expert evidence on the quantum of construction work.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L2; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1, L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Capital allowances
description: Tax depreciation and grants for capital spending (capital cost allowance in Canada, MACRS and cost segregation in the US): identifying qualifying expenditure, classifying assets and preparing claims.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of tax depreciation and incentives for capital spending on property, such as capital cost allowance in Canada or cost recovery deductions in the US, and related grants.
l2: Apply knowledge to practical capital allowances work including document collection, entitlement verification, and expenditure quantification.
l3: Provide reasoned advice on capital allowances strategy, prepare comprehensive claims, and negotiate with tax authorities.
l4: Advises on major capital cost allowance or cost segregation claims, negotiates with the CRA or IRS, or gives expert evidence on asset classification.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Due diligence
description: Due diligence: forensic examination of cost, quality and time, and of an asset or project's risks before a transaction or decision.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge of the techniques used to examine cost, quality and schedule in detail in your field, including the main risks to a lender or client and how contract documents and pricing data are reviewed.
l2: Apply due diligence investigation techniques to real property transactions and projects, conducting forensic examinations and reporting findings.
l3: Provide expert due diligence advice, lead complex investigations, assess and quantify risks, and advise clients on transaction decisions based on forensic examination findings.
l4: Leads due diligence on major transactions or projects for parties beyond their own firm, or gives expert evidence on what a competent investigation should have found.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Project feasibility analysis
description: Testing a project's feasibility: the feasibility study process, development appraisal, planning and financial viability.
l1: Describe how a feasibility study is carried out, including the financial and land-use planning sides of a development pro forma.
l2: Prepare development appraisals and feasibility studies, conduct sensitivity analysis, and support viability assessments.
l3: Provide strategic advice on development viability, community benefits charges, parkland and development charges, complex site appraisals, alternative financing structures, and sustainability impacts on feasibility.
l4: Advises on viability for major schemes and develops feasibility methods others use (for example municipal viability testing for inclusionary zoning or development charges).
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Housing maintenance, repairs and improvements
description: Maintaining, repairing and improving housing stock: the roles of owners, tenants and housing providers, funding and maintenance programmes.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the roles of owners, tenants, housing providers and municipalities in housing maintenance; funding for repairs and improvements; the building code, residential tenancy maintenance duties and municipal property standards; and planned versus reactive maintenance.
l2: Apply your knowledge to assess housing condition (building condition assessments, unit inspections), identify property-standards and health and safety hazards, prepare repair estimates and condition reports, and run maintenance programmes and contractors.
l3: Provide reasoned advice on maintenance strategy and capital priorities for housing portfolios, repair versus replacement on whole-life cost, compliance with property standards and tenancy obligations, and funding of improvement programmes.
l4: Sets capital repair and maintenance policy for large housing providers (building condition assessments, capital plans), or advises governments on housing repair standards and funding.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L2; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11)

name: Housing management and policy
description: Housing management and policy: the legislation and regulation of housing (residential tenancy law, social housing rules), tenancy management, and forming and implementing policy.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the legislation that governs housing management, including residential tenancy law (for example Ontario's Residential Tenancies Act), provincial housing services acts and US fair housing law; provincial social housing rules and HUD rules for US public housing; the political, economic and social context of housing across all tenures; and housing management standards and codes of practice.
l2: Carry out everyday housing management functions, including enforcing tenancy agreements, leases or licenses and applying residential tenancy legislation and regulatory guidance.
l3: Provide reasoned advice on housing management policy and good practice: prepare and present reports on forming and implementing policy, advise on standards, contribute to policy development, and give strategic guidance on housing management matters.
l4: Shapes housing management policy for providers or governments (residential tenancy rules, social housing access) and is consulted beyond their own organisation.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Market appraisal
description: Appraising the likely sale price or rent of property for marketing and pricing advice: comparable evidence, local market trends, the methods and standards that apply, and how such advice differs from a formal valuation.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of why opinions of market value or rent are prepared for sale or leasing, the methods and techniques used, the standards and guidance that apply, and especially the limits of such advice.
l2: Prepare market opinions of value for both sale and leasing, analyzing comparable evidence, using suitable methods, applying the relevant standards and guidance, and taking a detailed part in preparing and presenting client reports.
l3: Prepare client reports based on local market trends, investment proposals in the area, and the likely availability and terms of finance for the local market during construction and for future buyers.
l4: Sets market appraisal methods or pricing guidance others in their market use (comparable selection, list-price and rent strategy), or gives expert evidence on achievable price or rent.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1, L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Local taxation/assessments
description: Property tax at the municipal level: how assessors (MPAC in Ontario, US county assessors) value property, the basis of assessment, and reconsideration requests and appeals to bodies such as the Assessment Review Board.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how real estate, equipment and other property is taxed at the municipal or local level, including property tax assessment, the governing statutes and case law, and the valuation methods used.
l2: Apply knowledge of local taxation provisions to practical property assessment work.
l3: Provide expert professional advice on local taxation matters, including complex property assessments, strategic appeals, and tribunal representation.
l4: Leads precedent-setting assessment appeals whose decisions are cited, or advises assessment agencies, municipalities or legislators on assessment methods and policy.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L2; L3: reworded for North American practice and the level scale after review (2026-11-11); L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Valuation of businesses and intangible assets
description: Valuing businesses and intangible assets (brands, intellectual property, goodwill) for financial reporting, transactions, tax and litigation, using income, market and asset approaches under CBV Institute, AICPA or IVS standards.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of why businesses and intangible assets are valued, the methods and techniques used, the applicable standards and guidance, and any statutory or mandatory requirements for this work.
l2: Apply business valuation methods and techniques and the relevant standards, with detailed involvement in preparing and presenting client reports. You need not value businesses full time.
l3: Value businesses and their component parts competently for varied purposes, such as financial reporting, internal management, purchase or sale, tax and litigation, across different types and sizes of business, applying the methods and standards that govern the work.
l4: Gives expert evidence on business or intangible value in court, or contributes to valuation standards (CBV Institute, AICPA, ASA, IVS).
source: L1-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025), shortened for the graph; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Asset identification and assessment
description: Identifying and assessing a business's assets separately, tangible and intangible, for valuation and other purposes.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of principles of asset identification and assessment in business valuation contexts.
l2: Demonstrate practical application of asset identification and assessment in business valuation assignments, including analyzing legal documents, interpreting comparable evidence, and estimating asset lifespan.
l3: Provide reasoned advice to clients on how assets are separately identified for different purposes, including complex asset identification issues and intellectual property distinctions.
l4: Advises on complex intangible and IP identification (purchase price allocation, transfer pricing) and shapes valuation practice beyond their own firm.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph

name: Valuation reporting and research
description: Valuation reports and the research behind them: analysing, interpreting and validating information and inputs.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of what valuation reports are and the context they serve, and of how research is analyzed and information is interpreted and validated.
l2: Apply valuation reporting and research skills to analyze and interpret key appraisal inputs, use benchmarking techniques, and take account of the context in which a valuation is used.
l3: Give reasoned advice on valuation reports, standards and methodologies, and on validating and interpreting inputs and data.
l4: Sets reporting standards or templates others use, reviews others' valuations as a USPAP or CUSPAP review appraiser, or gives expert evidence on report adequacy.
source: L1-L3: RICS guide (Dec 2025); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Taxation
description: Taxation of different classes of assets: the statutory framework, general criteria and the valuations that support tax positions.
l1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how different classes of assets are taxed, including the governing statutes, general criteria and key provisions in your jurisdiction.
l2: Apply knowledge of taxation to practical valuation work, understanding specific tax requirements and how they differ from other valuation purposes.
l3: Provide strategic advice on complex tax valuation matters, negotiate with tax authorities, and handle sophisticated tax-related valuation issues.
l4: Settles major tax valuations with tax authorities (property transfer, estate, income tax) and gives expert evidence before tax courts or boards.
source: L1-L3: RICS-APC-prep; description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Ethics and professional responsibility in a digital environment
description: Ethical, legal and professional responsibilities in digital and data work, where digital outputs influence built environment decisions, markets or the public interest.
l1: Demonstrate understanding of the ethical principles that apply to using data, including fairness, transparency, privacy and professional conduct, and of privacy legislation such as PIPEDA or state privacy laws.
l2: Handle data responsibly in practice: follow ethical and professional standards whenever you manage, analyze or share data used for decisions about buildings, land or infrastructure.
l3: Advise on, or put in place, ethical digital and data practices in a professional setting that build trust and keep professionals accountable.
l4: Shapes professional guidance on data and AI ethics in the built environment (RICS standards on responsible AI use, professional codes), or advises regulators on automated valuation and data use.
source: L1-L3: RICS pilot guide (Sep 2026); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Data governance and data operations
description: Governing and operating data for trusted decisions: ownership, stewardship, quality assurance, standards, identifiers and interoperability.
l1: Understand how data is governed and managed: who owns and stewards it, how it is looked after through its life cycle, what makes it good quality, and why standards and unique identifiers matter.
l2: Put data governance and quality controls into practice so that the data behind real estate, infrastructure or environmental work is fit for its use, dependable, available to those who need it and compliant.
l3: Advise on or shape data governance and data management approaches that give professionals and clients confidence in built environment data.
l4: Sets data governance frameworks adopted beyond their own organisation and contributes to industry data standards (OSCRE, RESO, ISO 19650 information requirements).
source: L1-L3: RICS pilot guide (Sep 2026); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2, L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Data analytics and insight
description: Analysing, interpreting and communicating data to produce insight that informs professional judgement, from descriptive to predictive and model-based analysis.
l1: Understand core analytical concepts and their limits, and how clear communication turns data into insight for real estate and built environment decisions.
l2: Use analytical methods to produce insights that support specific built or natural environment decisions, communicate them clearly, and exercise professional judgment and accountability for the results.
l3: Advise on using data analytics and insight to shape built and natural environment decisions within your own professional field, explaining clearly how the data led to a particular outcome or decision.
l4: Develops analytical methods others adopt in the built environment (indices, automated valuation models, forecasting models), publishes them, or leads industry analytics practice.
source: L1-L3: RICS pilot guide (Sep 2026); description and L4: drafted for the graph; L1, L2: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15); L3: reworded for North American practice from the RICS guide's meaning and the pathway guides' examples (2026-11-15)

name: Data and digital practice across the built and natural environment life cycle
description: The role of data across the built and natural environment life cycle: depth in your own stage, and how the data you inherit and hand on affect other stages.
l1: Understand what data does across the life cycle of built and natural assets, including the main asset types, life-cycle stages, stakeholders and regulatory settings, and how it informs decisions on planning, delivering, operating, valuing and investing in those assets.
l2: Use your understanding of data across the asset life cycle in data-driven analysis, reporting or advisory work, showing how the use of data changes from stage to stage and influences the decisions made at each.
l3: Advise decision-makers or clients on decisions that rely on data and on digital systems, for projects, portfolios or organizations, taking into account the neighboring and wider life-cycle stages that bear on the decision.
l4: Shapes data practice across the life cycle for an organisation or industry (handover standards, data sharing between design, operation and valuation) and advises others on joining it up.

name: Cybersecurity and digital resilience
description: Digital risk, information security and the resilience of data systems and connected assets: confidentiality, integrity, availability and recovery from disruption.
l1: Understand cyber threats to data systems and connected building systems (operational technology, sensors, remote access), how threat, vulnerability and impact combine as risk, and the privacy duties that apply.
l2: Apply security controls (access management, encryption, network segmentation, patching, monitoring), record and assess digital risks to assets, and contribute to backup, recovery and incident-response plans.
l3: Advise on cyber, digital-risk and business-continuity strategy against the organisation's risk appetite and regulation; prioritise investment in controls; explain cyber risk to senior leaders in business terms.
l4: Sets cyber security strategy for portfolios with connected building systems (NIST Cybersecurity Framework, IEC 62443 for operational technology) or contributes to industry guidance.

name: Geospatial data and GIS
description: Spatial data and GIS for decisions about land, planning, the environment and assets: data types, coordinate reference, accuracy and spatial analysis.
l1: Understand the principles of GIS, spatial data and mapping, including data types, structures and formats, and how land and environmental spatial datasets are brought together.
l2: Use geospatial tools to analyze and combine spatial datasets, especially those for land use and environmental planning, including specifying data capture and sourcing suitable datasets.
l3: Advise clients on geospatial analysis and on integrating spatial data to support land and environmental strategies, from defining user requirements and data standards to presenting findings.
l4: Sets geospatial data strategy and standards for organisations or the industry (OGC standards, spatial data infrastructure) and advises others on spatial data risk.

name: Information management in construction and the built and natural environment
description: Managing asset and project information across the life cycle: defining, structuring, exchanging and handing over information to agreed standards.
l1: Understand the principles of information management as they apply to buildings, infrastructure and land.
l2: Manage information and use data-driven methods in practice on buildings, infrastructure or land, for example to inform design, benchmark assets or analyze performance.
l3: Advise on best practice for managing information across an organization or a project, including standards, shared data environments and responsibilities.
l4: Sets information management standards for organisations or programmes (ISO 19650 information requirements, COBie handover) and contributes to industry standards.

name: Data-driven valuation and risk analysis
description: Bringing data and analytical methods into valuation, appraisal and risk assessment within valuation standards, testing assumptions, sensitivities and limits.
l1: Understand how data shapes valuations and the assessment of investment risk.
l2: Support valuation and risk decisions with data in practice, using analytical models and datasets such as automated valuation models and market data analysis.
l3: Advise on valuation or investment risk strategies that are led by data.
l4: Develops valuation models or AVM methods others adopt, validates them for lenders or regulators, or contributes to valuation standards on data use.

name: Digital transformation strategy and innovation management
description: Managing and delivering digital transformation and innovation so that digital change is proportionate, ethical and delivers value while managing risk and legacy constraints.
l1: Understand the drivers of digital transformation in the built and natural environment, digital business models and tools, their organisational impacts, and the risks of digital adoption.
l2: Deliver digital initiatives, applying change management and supporting people through digital change, to achieve the outcomes an organization or client has defined.
l3: Advise on digital or data transformation strategies that serve a project's or organization's objectives: set the measures of success, provide governance and assurance, and step in when an initiative fails to deliver value or brings unacceptable risk.
l4: Leads digital transformation at organisation or industry level with results others cite, and advises boards of other organisations on digital investment and its governance.

name: Sustainability and ESG data
description: Using sustainability and ESG data for environmental performance, reporting, investment and sustainability strategy, including frameworks such as GRESB and ISSB.
l1: Understand ESG metrics and market data sources, and how sustainability considerations are built into decision-making, including frameworks such as GRESB and energy benchmarking programs.
l2: Work with ESG metrics and market data in practice, analyzing them to support decisions on investment, disclosure and sustainability performance.
l3: Advise on bringing ESG data into an organization's decisions and on the sustainability strategies that follow from it.
l4: Shapes ESG reporting frameworks or benchmarks (GRESB, ISSB or Canada's CSSB standards), or advises investors and regulators on ESG data.

name: Smart assets and digital twins
description: Smart building technologies and digital twins: real-time operational data, monitoring, simulation and digital replicas to improve asset performance and decisions.
l1: Understand what smart building systems and digital twins are for, their core concepts, and how data flows through them.
l2: Use smart technologies and digital twins to improve building operations or asset management, for example through building automation, sensor data and predictive maintenance.
l3: Advise on adopting smart building technologies and digital twins strategically, so that they shape long-term asset strategies.
l4: Sets smart asset and digital twin strategy for major portfolios or cities, or contributes to industry standards on twin data and interoperability.
